records.text: Israel sent a Mossad agent who led four or five bomb attacks on Jewish synagogues and communities in Iraq, after which 150,000 Jews moved to Israel within about a year and a half.
records.speaker: Bassem Youssef

appearances.snippet: Israel sends a Mossad agent and then he leads four to five different bomb attacks on Jewish synagogues and Jewish communities. ... They killed their own people. ... and that happened in Iraq and then because of that 150,000 Jews went in just like a year and a half. ... to Israel.

verification.notes: Historical sources support that Zionist underground agents were implicated in several Baghdad bombings and that the attacks contributed to Iraqi Jewish fear and emigration, but responsibility remains disputed and estimates are closer to 120,000–130,000 emigrants than 150,000. The exact claim of one Mossad agent directing four or five attacks is not established.

sources.relevance: Reviews the disputed evidence about Zionist involvement in the Baghdad bombings and the scale of Iraqi Jewish emigration.

records.text: Hillary Clinton sought the location of Gilgamesh's tomb a few days before the United States invaded Iraq.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Do you guys ever wonder why Hillary Clinton in those WikiLeak emails was asking a few days before we invaded Iraq, she was trying to locate Gilgamesh's tomb.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The email about locating Gilgamesh's tomb was a 2018 Freedom of Information Act request sent to the State Department by requester Denetra Senigar; it was not a directive or search request from Hillary Clinton. It also came fifteen years after the 2003 invasion of Iraq, not shortly before it.

sources.title: Lead Stories: Hillary Clinton and the Gilgamesh FOIA email
sources.relevance: Identifies the document as a private citizen's 2018 FOIA request and directly contradicts both the attribution to Clinton and the pre-invasion timing.

records.text: The United States killed a million Iraqis after lying about weapons of mass destruction.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That's how you kill a million Iraqis by just lying and saying they're weapons of mass destruction. No, they just mass murdered people,

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The central premise is supported: the invasion was sold with false claims about active Iraqi weapons-of-mass-destruction stockpiles, and the war caused hundreds of thousands of direct deaths plus larger indirect harms. However, 'the United States killed a million Iraqis' collapses disputed excess-mortality estimates, direct violent deaths, indirect deaths, and perpetrator attribution into one categorical number. The million figure is a contested high-end estimate, not a settled direct U.S. kill count.

sources.title: World Health Organization: Iraq violent-death estimate
sources.relevance: Authoritative estimate illustrates that direct violent-death totals and attribution differ materially from the categorical one-million formulation.

sources.title: CIA: Iraq Survey Group and WMD findings
sources.relevance: Supports the failure to find the alleged WMD stockpiles that were central to the invasion case.

records.text: We invaded just after Gilgamesh was found.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: Yes, we invaded just after he was found.

verification.notes: Transcript places the alleged discovery immediately before the 2003 invasion. A BBC report dated April 29, 2003 described a possible tomb match, after the March invasion began, while the underlying geophysical fieldwork occurred before the war. The chronology and certainty in the statement are therefore materially misleading.

sources.title: Gilgamesh tomb believed found
sources.relevance: April 29, 2003 report postdates the invasion and records only a tentative identification.

sources.relevance: Primary research paper establishes that the underlying prospecting began in 2001.

records.text: The first place that U.S. forces went during the Iraq War and set up a base was a museum that held relics, Babylonian cuneiform tablets, and Gilgamesh's tomb.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: The first place that we went during that war and set up a base was a museum. Not just any museum, the museum that held all of the relics. licks for that. It also held all the cuneiform tablets from Babylon and Gilgamesh and or Nimrod's tomb.

verification.notes: Transcript asserts that the museum/relic site was the first destination and base of U.S. forces. Current institutional records show Camp Alpha was established at Babylon after the invasion, but do not show it was the first place U.S. forces went; the Gilgamesh work was at Uruk, a different site. The composite claim is false.

sources.title: Report on Damage Assessments in Babylon
sources.relevance: UNESCO documents the later military base at Babylon but does not support the first-destination allegation.

sources.title: German Archaeological Institute - Uruk (Warka)
sources.relevance: Official project page locates the Gilgamesh-related prospecting at Uruk, not the Babylon museum/base.

records.text: In 2002, German geophysicists began trips into Iraq to map an ancient site aligned with the Gilgamesh texts.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: a group of German geophysicists began making trips into modern day Iraq to map out what they believe they had discovered, which was ancient Iraq that aligned with the ancient texts of Gilgamesh.

verification.notes: Transcript context is clear. The German Archaeological Institute's Uruk project and its primary paper document magnetic prospecting tests in 2001 and continued fieldwork in 2002, not a project that began only with trips in 2002. The statement's start date is false.

sources.title: Uruk - City of Gilgamesh: First tests in 2001 for magnetic prospecting
sources.relevance: Primary paper dates the first magnetic-prospecting tests to 2001, refuting a 2002 start.

records.text: Colin Powell publicly stated that Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction during an address to the United Nations Security Council.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Colin Powell publicly states, rather notoriously now infamously states, that Iraq possessed weapons of mass destruction. He's holding up the anthrax. He's addressing the United Nations Security Council.

verification.notes: Transcript context matches the historical claim. Official U.N. and U.S. State Department records confirm that Secretary of State Colin Powell addressed the Security Council on February 5, 2003 and presented the U.S. case that Iraq retained weapons of mass destruction.

sources.title: US Secretary of State Powell Presents Evidence of Iraq's Failure to Disarm
sources.relevance: Official U.N. record confirms Powell's February 5, 2003 Security Council WMD presentation.

records.text: A million Iraqi civilians were killed in the Iraq War.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: a million Iraqi civilians, civilians that were killed,

verification.notes: Transcript asserts one million Iraqi civilian deaths as settled fact. A survey-based ORB estimate approached one million, but Iraq Body Count and Brown University's Costs of War document roughly 187,000-211,000 violent civilian deaths, and later peer-reviewed analysis identifies major anomalies in the ORB survey. The figure is disputed, not established.

sources.title: Iraq Body Count
sources.relevance: Maintains a documented range of roughly 187,000-211,000 violent civilian deaths, far below one million.

sources.title: The violent death toll from the Iraq War: 2003-2023
sources.relevance: Peer-reviewed analysis explains anomalies affecting the near-million ORB survey estimate.

records.text: A senior U.S. military officer was willing to apologize for damage his troops caused at one of Iraq's most famous ancient sites.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #2 (Ep QRS_hR7NXaQ)

appearances.snippet: It tells us that a senior U.S. military officer has said that he's willing to apologize for damage that his troops caused in one of Iraq's most famous ancient sites.

verification.notes: Transcript context matches contemporary reporting. A senior U.S. officer, Colonel John Coleman, publicly said he was willing to apologize for damage caused by military occupation of Babylon while disputing some allegations.

sources.title: US colonel offers Babylon apology
sources.relevance: Reports Colonel John Coleman saying he was willing to apologize for military damage at Babylon.

Well, in 2005, the now bankrupt company, 23andMe came together where people began sending in those DNA kits to figure out their ancestry.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. 23andMe official corporate materials and an SEC filing date the company to 2006, not 2005. Operation Iraqi Freedom began in March 2003, so the specific founding-year claim is false; shortly afterward is subjective.

sources.title: 23andMe Holding Co. SEC Form 10-K
sources.relevance: Official filing dates the predecessor company incorporation to 2006.

records.text: The United States extracted Gilgamesh's tomb roughly two years after invading Iraq in 2003.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Okay. So we invaded, as I mentioned yesterday, mid 2003, and we extracted Gilgamesh, Gilgamesh's tomb roughly two years later.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. Contemporary archaeology reporting described geophysical evidence of structures that might correspond to a grave, not an excavated tomb or body. The German Archaeological Institute says war interrupted the work and large areas remained unexcavated; no credible evidence supports a later U.S. extraction.

records.speaker: Rob Skiba

appearances.snippet: 2003, the body of Gilgamesh was found in the desert of Iraq.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. The 2003 Uruk story concerned magnetometer-detected structures that an archaeologist cautiously said might resemble the epic description; no Gilgamesh body was found or excavated. Later viral body and mummy claims have been specifically debunked.

records.text: The United States established 500 military bases and the world's largest embassy in Babylon after invading Iraq under false pretenses.
records.speaker: Rob Skiba

appearances.snippet: We all know we went into Iraq under false pretenses, right? They told us weapons of mass destruction, right? They said that we didn't find weapons of mass destruction, but I have a feeling we found the weapon of mass destruction and we set up shop there immediately after that and established 500 military bases in the largest embassy of any other embassy on the entire planet in Babylon.

verification.notes: Transcript reviewed. Government records support that the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad was described as the world largest, but it is in Baghdad rather than ancient Babylon. GAO counted 311 U.S. installations in May 2008 and 283 in November 2008, not 500; false pretenses is an evaluative characterization.

sources.relevance: Reports 311 U.S. installations in May 2008, contradicting the 500-base figure.

sources.relevance: Government hearing record describes the Baghdad embassy as the largest in the world.

records.text: The United States urged citizens to leave Iraq after a drone struck the Baghdad embassy complex following strikes that killed three Kata'ib Hizballah members and reportedly wounded its leader.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This is real. U.S. urges citizens to leave Iraq after attack on the embassy in Baghdad because security officials say the embassy complex was struck by a drone after strikes killed three members of the Iran-backed Kata'ib Hezbollah and reportedly wounded its leader.

verification.notes: Transcript context at 34:19 summarizes a current news report. Contemporary reporting confirms that the embassy urged U.S. citizens to leave Iraq immediately after a drone struck the Baghdad embassy complex, following strikes that killed three Kata'ib Hezbollah members; reports that leader Ahmad al-Hamidawi was wounded were explicitly unverified. The statement preserves that 'reportedly' qualifier.

sources.title: US urges citizens to leave Iraq after attack on embassy in Baghdad
sources.relevance: Contemporary agency-based report confirms the alert, drone strike, three deaths, and qualified report that the leader was wounded.

sources.title: Iraq Travel Advisory | U.S. Department of State
sources.relevance: Official advisory confirms the ordered departure and severe security warning for U.S. citizens in Iraq.
